blocks.title: Rate law
blocks.text: The representation of the rate of a reaction in terms of the concentrations of the reactants is the rate law: an equation relating the rate to the concentrations of the reactants raised to various powers according to the experimental data.

For a general reaction aA + bB giving cC + dD the rate equation is rate = k [A]^x [B]^y, where x and y are experimentally determined values that may or may not equal the coefficients a and b of the balanced equation. The brackets stand for molar concentrations and the proportionality constant k is the rate constant. If [A] = 1 mol dm-3 and [B] = 1 mol dm-3, the rate = k x 1^x x 1^y = k.

blocks.title: Rate constant
blocks.text: The specific rate constant of a chemical reaction is the rate of reaction when the concentrations of the reactants are unity. Under given conditions k remains constant, but it changes with temperature.
